import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "gamma": 0.97, "gae_lambda": 0.95}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "gamma": 0.97, "gae_lambda": 0.95}

STEM = 48
W = 32
LW = 24
PROJ = 16
HID = 16


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, W, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.layer_in = nn.Conv2d(W + 13, LW, 1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(LW, PROJ, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * PROJ, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 2, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W + 2 * LW, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        lay = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        below = F.pad(lay, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :, :Z]
        above = F.pad(lay, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))[:, :, 1:]
        zc = torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype) / max(Z - 1, 1)
        zc = zc.view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        fz = f.unsqueeze(2).expand(B, f.shape[1], Z, Y, X)
        h = torch.cat([fz, lay, below, above, zc], dim=1)
        h = h.permute(0, 2, 1, 3, 4).reshape(B * Z, -1, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.layer_in(h))
        p = self.proj(h)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            o = out(F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1))))
            o = o.reshape(B, Z, 2, Y, X)
            gate = torch.softmax(o[:, :, 0], dim=1)
            score = (gate * o[:, :, 1]).sum(1)
            res.append(score.flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(res, dim=1)
        hz = h.reshape(B, Z, LW, Y, X)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)),
                                 hz.mean((1, 3, 4)), hz.amax((1, 3, 4))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "gamma": 0.97, "gae_lambda": 0.95}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 24
HID = 32


class CellHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        ins = []
        for dy, dx in self.fps:
            n = dy * dx
            ins.append(proj * n + (2 * proj if n > 1 else 0))
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(i, hid, 1) for i in ins])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        Y, X = p.shape[2], p.shape[3]
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                z = p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                cells = [q[:, :, i:i + Y, j:j + X] for i in range(dy) for j in range(dx)]
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                z = torch.cat(cells + [mx, mn], dim=1)
            res.append(out(F.relu(mix(z))))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)

            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.bcast = nn.Linear(64, WIDTH)
        self.head = CellHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob2 = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH + 64, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f2 = F.relu(f + self.bcast(g)[:, :, None, None])
        place = self.head(f2)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "gamma": 0.97, "gae_lambda": 0.95}

STEM = 48
W = 40
HEADS = 4
FF = 80
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d, heads, ff):
        super().__init__()
        self.heads = heads
        self.dh = d // heads
        self.n1 = nn.LayerNorm(d)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(d, 3 * d)
        self.o = nn.Linear(d, d)
        self.n2 = nn.LayerNorm(d)
        self.ff1 = nn.Linear(d, ff)
        self.ff2 = nn.Linear(ff, d)

    def forward(self, t):
        B, N, d = t.shape
        h = self.n1(t)
        qkv = self.qkv(h).reshape(B, N, 3, self.heads, self.dh).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        q, k, v = qkv[0], qkv[1], qkv[2]
        a = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-1, -2)) / math.sqrt(self.dh), dim=-1)
        y = torch.matmul(a, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, N, d)
        t = t + self.o(y)
        t = t + self.ff2(F.relu(self.ff1(self.n2(t))))
        return t


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels + 2, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, W, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.block = Block(W, HEADS, FF)
        self.head = PoolHead(W, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        cy = ys.view(1, 1, Y, 1).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        cx = xs.view(1, 1, 1, X).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        s = self.stem(torch.cat([obs, cy, cx], dim=1))
        f = F.relu(s + self.c1(s))
        t = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        t = self.block(t)
        f = F.relu(t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, -1, Y, X))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 2, "gamma": 0.97, "gae_lambda": 0.95}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32
VW = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Critic(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, cin):
        super().__init__()
        self.s = nn.Conv2d(cin, VW, 1)
        self.c = nn.Conv2d(VW, VW, 3, padding=1)
        self.fc = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * VW, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, 1))

    def forward(self, obs):
        h = F.relu(self.s(obs))
        h = F.relu(h + self.c(h))
        return self.fc(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)).squeeze(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.critic = Critic(spec.in_channels)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.critic(obs)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no results yet, and scores stay hidden for the whole search, so later rounds won't show which ideas worked. Each of the 3 candidates is therefore a strong bet on its own, not a single-change test. The starting recipe gets only about 32 PPO updates of 4,096 samples each. Halving n_envs to 128 doubles the number of updates without using any more samples. Raising gamma and lambda carries the +1 end-of-episode bonus further back through episodes of up to 33 steps. On the network side, the hard part is the landing layer, which is set by the highest filled cell under the footprint. Choosing a brick means comparing the build and target at that one layer and checking the columns below it. Two networks make this easy to learn while keeping compute close to the starting network's (r about 1), so the sample budget isn't cut: one scores each layer separately, and the other gives the action head each cell's own features plus a global summary.
analyses.2: Scores are hidden, so round 1 tells us only that all three files trained cleanly at r≈1. Nothing can be ranked yet, so this round tests three separate ideas. The task is mostly local: whether a brick lands right depends on the tallest column under its footprint and on whether target cells at that layer are missing and safe to cover. Placement order is mostly local too, because supports must sit under overhangs. That points to giving the action head more capacity rather than widening the view of the 2D trunk. The budget of about 131k steps is very small, so trading PPO epochs for more fresh designs is another strong lever. Global context (attention) is the one major idea not yet covered; it might help the DONE decision and placement order. The three candidates: (1) recipe only, ppo_epochs 2 on the baseline network; (2) r1c3 with one 3x3 convolution traded for a deeper per-footprint head; (3) a new design with a global attention block.
analyses.3: Scores are hidden, so no trial can be ranked on evidence. All six trials trained without errors at about 1.0–1.1x the starting compute, so r1c3 (cell-concat head) and r2c1 (baseline net, 2 PPO epochs) are both safe bases. Reasoning about the task: a brick is right only if its landing layer, which is the highest column under the footprint, matches the target cells exactly at that layer. That needs precise per-column information inside the footprint, which 3x3 trunk convolutions may blur. More fresh random designs (fewer PPO epochs) should help on held-out targets, but this is unverified. This round makes single changes to known-safe bases: (1) a skip link that feeds precise per-column stem features into the r1c3 head; (2) r1c3 with 2 epochs, mirroring r2c1; (3) a new idea, a separate critic so value-loss gradients do not disturb the policy features.
analyses.4: No scores are shown, so these choices rest on reasoning, not results. All 9 trials trained without errors, and the compute ratio r for every network stayed near 1, so there is room for small changes. Two ideas were tested separately but never together. One is the cell head with the stem skip (r3c1), which keeps exact per-column detail for each footprint cell. The other is 2 PPO epochs, which gives about 1.8x more fresh designs (r2c1, r3c2). Since there is no feedback and this is the last round, I am betting on combinations that each look reasonable, not on single-change tests. Combination 1: stem-skip cell head with 2 epochs. Combination 2: the same network with 1 epoch, which pushes sample count further (about 420k steps). Combination 3: add a dilated residual convolution, so every cell sees most of the 8x8 grid. That should help with placement order around overhangs and with DONE timing, at a modest cost.
